## 2. YouTube description (the first two lines are the hook shown before “more”)

### 2.1 English (main) — 2810 characters (limit 5000)

```text
Sample A crosses the line at cycle 22, sample B at 31. Which one had more target to begin with?
Real-time PCR on a schematic: the thermal cycler, the amplification curve and Cq — in under 75 seconds.

In this video:
• One PCR cycle: heat separates the strands, on cooling primers bind and a polymerase builds new strands — so the target roughly doubles every cycle (general principle).
• The thermal cycler on a schematic with numbered parts: tube strip, heated lid, and a Peltier block that switches temperatures.
• The optical path: excitation source, excitation filter, the tube, emission filter and detector.
• The amplification curve: fluorescence grows with the product; Cq is the cycle where it crosses the threshold — the lower the Cq, the more starting target.
• Two cautions: trace contamination can give false results, and no amplification does not prove a negative.
• Real LabGuide screens: Lab → Instruments and methods → Molecular diagnostics → Real-time PCR — the schematic, its numbered parts and the principle, each with its sources, then limitations and contamination control.

Chapters
0:00 Two samples and one PCR cycle
0:17 The thermal cycler and the optical path
0:32 Amplification curve, Cq and two cautions
0:49 In LabGuide: the Real-time PCR card

What LabGuide does today:
• LabGuide has a Real-time PCR reference card in Lab → Instruments and methods → Molecular diagnostics: the schematic with numbered parts and the principle, each with its sources.
• The card also covers limitations and contamination control.
• Reference cards: the assay IFU and your laboratory SOP decide.

Good to know:
• Schematic — not an exact model; the curves are illustrative, not a real assay or result.
• The assay IFU and your laboratory SOP decide thresholds and interpretation.
• A general-principle video, not an assay protocol; the card in the app is itself marked as not yet expert-reviewed.

LabGuide is a clinical-laboratory companion app for lab professionals and students (English, Russian, Uzbek). It is a learning and reference tool: it does not diagnose or interpret patient results. Works offline and without an account.
Get the app: [[LINK_APP_STORE]] · [[LINK_PLAY]]

Illustrative data — not patient results.
Educational use, not medical advice.
English synthetic narration (Kokoro-82M, Apache-2.0); English subtitles.
```

### 2.2 Русский — 2844 characters (limit 5000)

```text
Проба A пересекает линию на 22-м цикле, проба B — на 31-м. В какой было больше мишени?
ПЦР в реальном времени на схеме: термоциклер, кривая амплификации и Cq — меньше чем за 75 секунд.

В этом видео:
• Один цикл ПЦР: нагрев разделяет цепи, при охлаждении садятся праймеры, полимераза строит новые цепи — поэтому мишень почти удваивается за цикл (общий принцип).
• Термоциклер на схеме с пронумерованными частями: стрип, нагреваемая крышка и термоблок Пельтье, который переключает температуры.
• Оптический путь: источник возбуждения, фильтр возбуждения, пробирка, эмиссионный фильтр и детектор.
• Кривая амплификации: флуоресценция растёт с продуктом; Cq — цикл пересечения порога: ниже Cq — больше мишени в начале.
• Две оговорки: следовое загрязнение может дать ложный результат, а отсутствие амплификации ещё не доказывает отрицательный результат.
• Реальные экраны LabGuide: Лаб. → Приборы и методики → Молекулярная диагностика → ПЦР в реальном времени — схема, её пронумерованные части и принцип, у каждого источники, затем ограничения и защита от загрязнения.
```

## 10. End screen / CTA suggestion

* YouTube end screen (last ~7–20 s): subscribe + the next video in the SAME language edition (`gcms`, `osmometry`) + the playlist `[[LINK_PLAYLIST]]`. Place elements so they do not cover the end card's path pill or disclosure notices (check against the final scene).
* Description and pinned comment carry the store links (`[[LINK_APP_STORE]]`, `[[LINK_PLAY]]`); the video itself shows only the in-app path, no URL and no price.
* Instagram: link in bio (`[[LINK_BIO]]`); ask viewers to save/share, not to "download now".

## 11. Safe-content notes

* No patient data, names or real results anywhere. All numbers on screen are illustrative and labelled so.
* No third-party logo, brand name, stock footage or music. The only logo is the owner's app icon.
* Do not call the voice "natural", "professional" or "human": it is synthetic and nobody has listened to it yet.
* Do not call the content "approved", "verified", "certified" or "clinically validated": expert review is pending.
* No diagnosis, treatment, dosing or "normal range" statement. Reference ranges come from the user's laboratory.
* Do not answer individual medical questions in comments; point to the user's laboratory SOP, the reagent IFU and the clinician.
* No price, discount, product id or availability date in any text (docs/DECISIONS.md D-77/D-78: prices live in the stores).
* Check the platform's own disclosure setting for AI-generated / synthetic voice before posting (NEEDS_OWNER_CHECK: the rules change; the kit already states the voice is synthetic in the text).
* Audience: not made for kids. Category: Education. Comments: moderate; hide spam and requests for medical advice.
